notes: Not an eyewitness view. A retrospective reconstruction: Currey's plate follows a Chicago Daily Tribune drawing (5 March 1899) of a model Albert L. Van den Berghen built in 1898, nearly a century after the fort burned. Its numbered key names the main entrance (1), sally-port (2), western gateway (3), north-west and south-east blockhouses (4, 5), officers' quarters (6), barracks (7) and magazine (8). Where it departs from John Whistler's contemporary 1808 measured draught (which ranges stand where, the gate building, the blockhouse overhangs), the draught governs the model; this picture is shown for comparison. Joined to the 1812 fort's cards through the fort's diagnostic reference camera, with no Prairie parcel or building identity.
